text:
incident-bot: PagerAlert: HIGH - GPU pool exhaustion (us-east-1). Autoscaler hit max_nodes=48, queue growth observed. Impact: increased latency and 429s for some hosted API customers. See /alerts/RED-1123.

maya_ng: I'm on it — checking autoscaler logs and region routing.

sanjay_r: hitting 95% GPU utilization across the cluster. Queue length ~12k requests, avg wait time 18s. Throttling started at 2026-03-05T14:02Z.

liam_h: Confirmed autoscaler returned `scale_up_failed` events due to quota in us-east-1. Cloud provider refused additional GPUs.

alex_c: Is cross-region spillover enabled? I think the policy should route to eu-west-1 or us-west-2 when primary saturated.

maya_ng: Spillover policy is enabled but observed fallback to the wrong model family (v1-quant) in eu-west-1 which caused compatibility errors and subsequent retries. Logs: 
```
2026-03-05T14:03:12Z router ERROR route:spillover -> model_mismatch v1-quant vs expected rdx-3b-fp16
```

sanjay_r: Looks like the router used `model_variant:compatible` heuristic and matched an incompatible variant. That caused many requests to fail fast and requeue, worsening the backlog.

liam_h: Immediate mitigation idea: 1) temporarily increase fallback region weight to eu-west-1 for latency-tolerant tiers, 2) disable automatic variant coercion so only exact model matches are routed, 3) enable emergency throttling at 60% for non-SLAs. Thoughts?

maya_ng: Agree. I'll flip the routing weight and disable variant coercion. Executing admin commands now.

maya_ng: Executed: 
```bash
# bump eu-west weight for hosted-api routes
redwood-admin routing update --route hosted-api --policy spillover --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.7
# disable variant coercion globally (temp)
redwood-admin config set router.variant_coercion false --session incident-RED-1123
# emergency throttle for non-enterprise plans
redwood-admin quota set --plan free,starter --rate 60% --session incident-RED-1123
```

incident-bot: Action logs recorded: routing.weight_change, router.config_change, quota.update.

sanjay_r: After changes: queue reduced from 12k -> 4k over 6 minutes, 429 rate dropped 78% for enterprise customers. Latency for routed eu-west requests ~220ms extra but within SLO for tier=starter? need confirmation.

liam_h: Cloud quota team responded: we can request emergency quota but approval ETA 2-4 hours. Worth opening request but we need short-term ops.

alex_c: Support: customers with errors?

support_bot: Customer notify candidates: list compiled for impacted keys where >5% requests failed in window 14:00-14:10Z. Generating temporary status entries.

maya_ng: On-call handoff incoming in 20 minutes to @sanjay_r -> @liam_h. I'll document actions in the incident ticket.

sanjay_r: Taking first shift. Next steps: monitor queue length, verify eu-west capacity, start quota request, and prepare controlled rollout to us-west-2 if eu-west fills.

liam_h: Also suggest enabling prefix caching for high-retry customers to reduce recompute. I can toggle caching policy for a subset of routes.

maya_ng: Done for the top 6 noisy routes. Cache hit rate initial bump to 12%.

incident-bot: Update: mitigation in progress. Incident state: mitigated (partial). Root cause: primary region GPU quota exhaustion + router variant coercion causing incompatible fallbacks and requeues.

sanjay_r: Will keep monitoring and post final timeline + RCA draft. If anyone sees regression ping oncall.emoji :mega:

alex_c: Thanks team — solid triage. Please include recommendation: block incompatible variant coercion in default policies and add synthetic test for spillover correctness.

maya_ng: Noted for post-incident actions.

support_bot: Customer notifications drafted for status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-1123.

liam_h: Handing back to steady-state in 40m unless quotas come through.

incident-bot: Incident thread archived at 2026-03-05T15:15Z (will remain open for RCA).
